guest_events_utc.observation: Executor memcg usage and limit were both 262144 KiB; oom_group=0. Kernel selected the intended tool process awk (PID 1125, oom_score_adj=1000, RSS about 217472 KiB).

Before oom_reaper completed awk at 06:51:34.275Z, a second memcg OOM selected codex PID 414 (anonymous RSS about 41564 KiB), the native exec-server. It exited 137; no VM_EXEC_RESULT arrived, then the client observed websocket reset and unknown session.

pr_15741_tool_oom.causal_conclusion: The second kernel OOM kill explains the exec-server exit and transport/session loss. The evidence does not support a stale-session delete as the initial fault or a standalone websocket fault.
pr_15741_tool_oom.repair_boundary: Current follow-up disposition: existing OOM and no-replay assertions remain unchanged. The pinned bundled Codex 0.162.1 exec-server does not expose per-command memory/cgroup placement or pre-exec controls. The patch-dependent native fork route was rejected; PRs #15800 and #15869 were closed. The CLI supports CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_URL; replacing the executor is a separate architecture and ownership decision covering process, session, PTY, sandbox and filesystem behavior. The shared-cgroup OOM evidence remains valid; no exec-server-survival guarantee or runtime repair is established. Capability audit: https://github.com/agentydragon/ducktape/pull/15883.
pr_15741_tool_oom.raw_evidence: BuildBuddy invocation metadata, execution/test spans, guest console, journal and serial logs were inspected locally and are not published.
